To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the existing approaches to deal with the ambiguities in natural software requirements can be broadly classified into two categories: those that use formal specifications and those that use knowledge and ontology; (2) the approaches that use formal specifications are not suitable for mainstream software development; and (3) the approaches that rely on knowledge and ontology have been observed to yield better results.

(i) The prevalent approaches to resolve natural language ambiguities can be categorized into three broad categories, viz. (a) approaches that use natural language understanding, (b) approaches that use machine learning, and (c) approaches that use knowledge and ontologies; (ii) The prevalent approaches can be further sub-categorized into approaches that are automated, semi-automated, and manual; (iii) The prevalent approaches are used for resolving specific types of ambiguities in software requirements.
